Answer: B
Reason: The provided images illustrate the "deep interlobar fissure sign" or displacement of the azygos lobe. In the context of pneumothorax, air accumulates in the pleural space and can dissect into the azygos fissure, causing the azygos lobe to shift laterally away from the mediastinum. This results in an empty-appearing fissure without the typical teardrop-shaped opacity (which represents the cross-section of the azygos vein and surrounding tissue) at its caudal end, as described in option B.
